correctness.rationale: All quantifiers are explicit: each 2x2 real invertible matrix with a>b>0, q in nonnegative integers and ell>=1 iid sign columns, rank-revealing Q and target-rank-one truncated SVD. The two sign-line sampling outcomes partition the sample space; when both lines appear, Y is invertible and gives the optimal b^2 residual; otherwise each single-line projector yields the displayed exact rational energy. Event weights each equal 2^{-ell}. The concavity identity H=2-g(c)-g(1-c) proves and attains sharp global extrema, including equality boundaries. Worst sign-line alignment prevents q-repair, while rho→0 gives interior q-consistency; Gaussian ell>=2 has full rank almost surely. Standalone verify.py was executed from its actual path and printed 410 exact-rational identities; finite checks only supplement the universal analytic proof. No unverified nonstandard lemma or infinite computation is needed.

value.rationale: The object is the standard rank-one-truncated randomized SVD with iid ±1 sub-Gaussian sketches, as motivated by arXiv:2308.05814v1. The new result completely classifies a natural two-dimensional model by singular-frame orientation and every power depth, with attained best/worst expected squared errors. It reveals a structural obstruction that power iteration cannot remove—positive-probability omission of the leading singular line—and an exact logarithmic-in-condition-number sample-width criterion for uniform approximation. This is not an arbitrary numeric special case: it contrasts repeated power passes with independent sampling and with almost-sure Gaussian success. No claim about general matrices or new asymptotic algorithms is made.
